title: A three-job counterexample to input-order greedy scheduling
question: Does assigning each next job to the less-loaded of two identical machines always minimize the finish time?
method: Replay the fixed [2,2,3] witness with ties to machine 0, enumerate all eight assignments independently, and compare with the original Lotus packet.
finding: The stated greedy rule yields loads [5,2] and makespan 5. Assignment [0,0,1] yields [4,3] and makespan 4, which is optimal for this input.
claim_scope: One exact counterexample refutes universal optimality of this input-order rule. The finite optimum check covers all eight assignments of these three jobs to two machines.
limitations: Existing Lotus simulated-visitor demonstration; not a new discovery or evidence of external adoption.
No smallest-counterexample claim, characterization of all inputs, or evaluation of reordering heuristics.
No general runtime, SAT, or P-versus-NP conclusion.
open_questions: How would a separately specified rule that reorders jobs behave on an explicitly bounded domain?
